title: Admission and recovery — complete synthetic catalogue
lead: Move validation to the admission boundary, keep rejected input out of the stream, and make acceptance distinct from read visibility.
changes: Validate the command before the first publication side effect.
Return a clear rejection to the caller; keep the consumer focused on accepted events.
Document the changed interfaces, failure modes and operational signals. This entire PR is a synthetic example, not executed evidence.
Add Recovery with retained intent, unknown outcomes and conditional alternatives; no live recovery or passing-test claim.

references.label: Scope
references.value: Invented source, requirements, cases and outcomes; no repository, service or test execution is implied.

faults.title: Remove admission validation

sections.title: Acceptance is not read visibility
sections.reason: The API receipt and projected read model are separate. Timings below are illustrative, not measured.

states.label: Accepted
states.happened: Admission succeeds and a receipt is returned.
states.readReturns: 404 · the projection has not applied the event.

states.label: Published
states.happened: The accepted event is durable in the stream.
states.readReturns: 404 · stream durability is not read visibility.

states.label: Visible
states.happened: The consumer has applied the event and the reader observes it.

sections.title: Why validate here?
sections.reason: The chosen option, alternatives and accepted cost explain the boundary without claiming an independent review verdict.

decisions.question: Where should invalid commands stop?

options.label: Validate at admission
options.why: The caller gets a rejection before any publication side effect.

options.label: Keep validation in the consumer
options.why: A later rejection cannot retract an already published event.

options.label: Duplicate validation at both boundaries
options.why: Two policy owners would need coordinated rule changes.

decisions.tradeoff: Validation now adds work to the request path. This example makes no measured latency claim.

decisions.question: Should a receipt promise read visibility?

options.label: Acknowledge durable admission
options.why: Keep the API independent of projection lag.

options.label: Wait for the read model
options.why: Projection availability would become part of request success.

decisions.tradeoff: Callers must distinguish receipt from visibility and handle a temporarily absent read result.

sections.title: Delivery recovery ledger
sections.reason: Read the supplied evidence boundary before considering any conditional action. Unknown is not confirmed failure.

operations.title: Lost Complete response
operations.intent: Complete the existing synthetic delivery once; never replace its identity just because the response was lost.
operations.identity: delivery-synthetic-42; provider task provider-synthetic-7; the pinned revision remains revision-3. Repeated identity alone does not prove provider idempotency.

points.title: Response lost after Complete was sent
points.attempt: The Complete request was sent, but the owner restarted before receiving its response. Literal payload: <complete> </script><script>not executable</script> & unchanged.
known: The retained intent names the existing provider task.
The request was sent before the response channel was lost.
unknown: Whether a lost response contained an error or a successful receipt.
retained: Delivery identity delivery-synthetic-42 and pinned revision-3.
Uploaded object receipts upload-a and upload-b.
points.budget: 2 of 5 attempts used; original deadline retained

alternatives.when: If authoritative provider evidence confirms the same task is complete.
alternatives.result: Record the completion receipt for the pinned delivery without sending another Complete.

alternatives.when: If provider evidence confirms pending work and the retained policy permits another attempt.
alternatives.result: Resume completion for provider-synthetic-7 with the original identity, uploads and carried budget.

alternatives.when: If authoritative status remains unavailable or conflicting after the supplied recovery boundary.
alternatives.result: manual-recovery remains unresolved; the duty owner must reconcile provider-synthetic-7 before settlement. Literal note <pending> </script> is not a control.

prohibited: Do not turn unknown into confirmed-failure.
Do not create a new provider task or repeat completed uploads solely because a response is missing.

points.title: Matching provider completion evidence supplied
points.attempt: The author supplies a later authoritative completion receipt for the same provider task.
known: The supplied receipt names provider-synthetic-7 and revision-3.
retained: The original delivery identity and all upload receipts.

alternatives.when: If the receipt is accepted by the authored system's admission policy.
alternatives.result: Settle this delivery using the supplied receipt; this display does not verify it.

operations.title: Resume retained uploads
operations.intent: Finish the same delivery after an interrupted upload without discarding confirmed progress.
operations.identity: delivery-synthetic-42; object manifest manifest-synthetic-v3; the task and manifest remain pinned across continuation.

points.title: One upload attempt failed
points.attempt: The provider explicitly rejected upload-c. Receipts for upload-a and upload-b were retained before restart.
known: upload-a and upload-b have supplied retained receipts.
The upload-c attempt returned an explicit rejection.
retained: The completed upload-a and upload-b receipts.
points.budget: 2 of 5 attempts used; original deadline retained

alternatives.when: If the same manifest is still admitted and the carried policy permits the remaining upload.
alternatives.result: Upload only upload-c, retaining existing receipts and the original deadline.

alternatives.when: If the proposed continuation changes the pinned manifest or delivery identity.
alternatives.result: Reject the replacement request without claiming the wider delivery succeeded or failed.

prohibited: Do not repeat upload-a or upload-b.
Do not reset the carried budget, deadline or pinned identity.

operations.title: Bounded awareness handoff
operations.intent: Notify an observer about an already settled business result without changing that result.
operations.identity: notice-synthetic-8 names delivery-synthetic-42 and its existing business receipt; the notice is separate work.

points.title: Notice has not yet been attempted
points.attempt: The owner resumed with an authored pending notice, before any send attempt.
retained: The original business receipt and the separate notice identity.

alternatives.when: If the authored notice policy still admits a first send.
alternatives.result: Attempt the existing notice without rerunning the business delivery.

alternatives.when: If the supplied handoff policy has closed the notice window.
alternatives.result: Skip only this notice. The task's business outcome stays unchanged; no wider success or failure is invented.

prohibited: Do not reopen the settled business task to send a notice.
